title: data-labeling-guidelines-draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for refining the data labeling/cleanup guidelines for the customer-support-intent dataset. Goal is to codify label rules, capture frequent edge cases, and provide sample snippets for annotators and automated cleanup heuristics. NOT final - will iterate after sync with Ryan and QA team.

Scope:
- Short text inputs (<= 512 tokens) from chat transcripts, support emails, and in-app feedback.
- Primary labels: intent category (billing, account, bug, feature_request, cancellation, general_help), urgency (low/medium/high), contains_pii (yes/no), botable (yes/no - i.e., safe for automated response).

Label taxonomy - rough:
- intent: choose single best intent. If multiple intents, pick the primary or mark as multi_intent and add freeform note.
- urgency: high = explicit deadlines, legal/regulatory risk, or financial loss. Medium = user frustrated, repeated attempts. Low = informational.
- contains_pii: mark yes if any direct identifier (email, phone, account number) or strong personal data.
- botable: yes only if can be solved by canned flow w/o escalation.

Edge cases / heuristics:
1) Short vague: "It broke" -> label bug + low urgency unless user includes timeline or payment impact.
2) Implicit billing: "charged twice?" -> billing + urgency medium if recent transaction mentioned.
3) Multi-intent: "I want a refund and also the app crashes" -> prefer label = refund (billing) if user asks for refund as primary action; mark multi_intent.
4) PII in screenshots described as text: if user writes "see screenshot with card ending 4242" -> contains_pii=yes.
5) Non-English or heavy code-switching: flag for review (team: lang-specialist).
6) Offensive language: do not strip; label as general_help/bug/etc but add note if harassment present.

Examples (annotator samples):
- "I was charged twice for order #12345, please refund" => intent: billing, urgency: high, contains_pii: yes, botable: no (requires billing team).
- "How do I change my password?" => intent: account, urgency: low, contains_pii: no, botable: yes.
- "App crashes when I open settings after update" => intent: bug, urgency: medium, contains_pii: no, botable: no (needs triage).

Automated cleanup suggestions (pre-labeling passes):
- Normalize ticket/order ids (regex) and replace with token <ORDER_ID> for annotator clarity but keep contains_pii=Yes if id present in original.
- Collapse repeated punctuation/emojis to single token for intent detection.
- Remove auto-signatures ("Thanks, Sarah") only for intent labeling, but annotate original keep for PII detection.

QA checks for label consistency:
- Weekly random sample 200 items -> compute inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) on intent and urgency. Flag intents with kappa < 0.6 for guideline clarifications.
- Build a small set of golden examples (n=150) covering edge cases above for onboarding.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final list for intent taxonomy (Ryan to propose if we should split "account" into login/payment/profile).
- Agree threshold for 'botable' - do we allow partial botable where step 1 is bot and step 2 is human? (propose: botable=partial/yes/no?)
- How to handle feature_request vs product-feedback - current plan: merge into feature_request unless explicit feedback only.
- Need to add language labels and escalation rules for non-English.

Next actions:
- Merge notes into PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-data/pull/78 (assigned: Asha)
- Schedule 30m sync with Ryan + QA (todo: create calendar invite)
- Draft final guidelines doc and golden set by end of month.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc messy. Save examples as separate file samples-labeling-asha.csv once we have 200 cleaned rows.

----
Informal/brainstorm bits:
- consider a botable_score float (0-1) predicted by model to prefilter. If >0.8 auto-suggest response and send to review queue.
- think about auto-detecting "refund" verbs (refund, reimburse, chargeback) vs "billing" umbrella for better routing.
